loops.title: Hruday boundary decay of the AM2 creation coefficients for the named constructions
loops.accepted: In the AM2/AQ1 zero-selected patterned family (model AQ_patterned_zero_selected: SU(2) Kogut-Susskind form on Z^3 at fixed spacing, coarse 24-link factors, selected triple exactly (0,0,0) with Haar product reference, 21 omitted faces per anchor entering as -(tau/3)W_f in normalized units delta=alpha/8; both signs |tau|<=10^-8; AM2 creation expansion with J<=28|tau|, R=1/64, G(t)=16e^{8t}(1+10t); cover R={0,e_z}; coarse l-infinity metric with star diameter d_X=1), with the named construction families F1 = AQ1 centered whole-star boxes Lambda_N=[-N,N]^3 and F2 = I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding on the same Lambda_N, N at least 2: For the zero-selected patterned family at the same coupling |tau|<=10^-8, and for the named construction families F1 (centered whole-star boxes) and F2 (all-contained-face boxes with padding) on centered coarse cubes, the AM2 creation coefficients in each on-site cutoff space, on supports meeting the cover R, differ between two boxes of the named constructions by at most K q^(N-1) in the anchored norm, uniformly in the cutoff, where N is the smaller box size; this is decay of the coefficients of the named constructions at a rate in N, not decay of the reduced density, not a statement about untruncated creation coefficients, not uniqueness of any ground state, and not a statement uniform in the lattice spacing a. Constants (exact, both signs, every comparison of the contract: F1 on Lambda_N versus Lambda_(N+1), F2 on Lambda_N versus Lambda_(N+1), F1 versus F2 on the same Lambda_N, any two centered boxes of size at least N and any two complete-factor volumes of one prescription containing Lambda_N): headline pair q=1/64 with K=49/111790368 (about 4.3832e-7; exact_first_order tier, analytic_disc route on the disc of radius 64|tau|; margin about 1.1407 against the frozen 1/2000000), also certified by the weighted_norm route with the smaller K=2734375/12204185915601 (about 2.2405e-7, labelled); floor pair q=148/390625=37888|tau| with K=49/2018304 (about 2.4278e-5; exact_first_order tier, analytic_disc route on the disc of radius tau_star=1/37888), also certified by the weighted_norm route with K=708203125/43148545682688 (about 1.6413e-5, labelled). The crude_majorant tier at q=1/64 (296/390625 analytic_disc, 9472/24454143 weighted_norm) misses 1/2000000 and is retained. The tau to tau/100 ratios are 4340004/43129 for the headline K, exactly 1 for the floor K and exactly 100 for q_min. The rate is in N, per coarse l-infinity step at fixed spacing; every interaction term present in one box and not the other lies at coarse l-infinity distance at least N-1 from R, and the bound uses the contract form ceil(d/diam) of the order-versus-distance count. For each family the whole sequence of coefficients on supports meeting R is Cauchy in each on-site cutoff space; this is a coefficient statement only, with no state, reduced density, common limit or untruncated coefficient asserted.
loops.summary: A change of the box boundary moves the AM2 creation coefficients on supports meeting the Wilson cover by at most K q^(N-1): K about 4.4e-7 at q=1/64 and K about 2.4e-5 at the per-step ball ratio q=37888|tau| (about 3.8e-4 at the cap), for every comparison of the two named box constructions, at both signs and uniformly in the on-site cutoff; proved by a weighted-norm contraction and independently by analyticity on a complex coupling disc.
limitations: Only the zero-selected patterned family (selected triple (0,0,0), Haar reference), the cover R={0,e_z}, fixed spacing and |tau|<=10^-8, with F1 and F2 on centered cubes Lambda_N, N at least 2, and complete-factor volumes of one prescription containing Lambda_N; nothing transfers to nonzero selected triples, the uniform route-B model, literal vertex boxes, weak coupling or the continuum; every constant is uniform in N at fixed spacing and in the cutoff, never in a.

Coefficients only: the statements concern AM2 creation coefficients in each on-site cutoff space Q_L with constants independent of L; they are not decay of the reduced density or of any state (BB1/BB2), not a statement about untruncated creation coefficients, and the analyticity in the coupling is not extended to the reduced density (no zero-free region of the complexified normalization is proved).

The coefficient Cauchy property gives whole-sequence convergence of coefficients per cutoff space only; whole_sequence_claimed and common_limit_claimed concern states and stay false; no uniqueness of any ground state is asserted.

Thin headline margin: the bound headline K=49/111790368 is about 1.1407 below 1/2000000 (the freeze-time margin rule was checked against the forward preview only); the labelled refinements (reverse sharp exponent 49/7154583552, reverse first-order cancellation 3773/1364628515625 which is quadratic in tau, forward loss-one F1-versus-F2 value 57270955/16662781836767232) are recorded and not bound.

Exponent convention: the bound uses the contract form ceil(d/diam) (exponent N-1 at e_z for every comparison); the sharp count 1+ceil(d/diam) gives exponent N, but a floor constant written that way is linear in tau (ratio exactly 100) and falls outside the prefrozen floor bracket, so every sharp form is labelled.

General comparisons: the reverse compares any two volumes directly (constant K); telescoping at exponent N-1 would give 889/1006113312 and a two-step union 49/55895184, both above 1/2000000; the forward telescoped constant 2734375/12204185915601 and its union constant are valid labelled values; the face sets are totally ordered (F1_N inside F2_N inside F1_(N+1)), so one nested comparison suffices for any pair of centered boxes.

Contract wording read as follows: the source set of a nested comparison is the shell, and the literal set of sites met by the new terms adds the outer layer of Lambda_N (98, 218, 386 sites at N=2,3,4) at distance N-1 from e_z, which gives the same bound once the source loss is charged; the fixed-point map has Lipschitz constant J_0G'(R) below 77/781250, while 2J_0G'(R) is the AM2 exclusion constant; gate_fields_topic_specific is read as the 12 frozen gate fields; the floor difference weight is e^beta=w=390625/148.

Inherited without re-proof: the AM2 multilinear majorant, fixed point, uniqueness in the ball and cutoff facts; the AV1 exact first-order coefficient and self-consistent remainder; the AY1 item-by-item F2 premises; the I1 dictionary; Banach, Weierstrass and the maximum principle are standard and not machine-checked.

Independence is limited to routes, enumerations and code: the contract and selection note name both mechanisms, the skeptic triage proposed both routes and the frozen parameters, all agents are correlated model agents, and isolation is verified for repository inputs only.
Upper bounds only; the -tau values replay the same |tau| formula; scientific priority is unverified.
loops.model: Zero-selected patterned family (AQ_patterned_zero_selected) at both signs |tau|<=10^-8; AM2 creation expansion (J<=28|tau|, R=1/64, G(t)=16e^{8t}(1+10t)) in each on-site cutoff space uniformly in the cutoff; construction families F1 (AQ1 centered whole-star boxes) and F2 (I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding) on centered coarse cubes Lambda_N, N at least 2; cover R={0,e_z}; coarse l-infinity metric on factor sites (star diameter 1)
derivation_steps: Show the AM2 multilinear estimate and ball self-map survive in a diameter-weighted anchored norm with the loss paid once per interaction (forward), or for complex couplings on a disc (reverse, analyticity of the fixed point).
Prove the order-versus-distance lemma: a coefficient on a support meeting R depends on a term at coarse distance d only at order at least 1+ceil(d/diam), with the diameter convention enumerated.

Identify the boundary source of each comparison (the shell, the 28N(5N+1) extra F2 faces) and bound the coefficient difference by K q^(N-1) at both frozen pairs by the weighted contraction or by Cauchy's estimate.
applications: First step towards whole-sequence convergence of the named constructions (Round32 roadmap goals 1 and 3): the input to the marginal-locality lemma BB1.
Coefficient decay alone is not state decay; the normalization couples all supports (BB1).

loops.title: Hruday boundary comparison of the Heisenberg dynamics of the named constructions on compact windows
loops.accepted: In the AM2/AQ1 zero-selected patterned family (model AQ_patterned_zero_selected: SU(2) Kogut-Susskind form on Z^3 at fixed spacing, coarse 24-link factors, selected triple exactly (0,0,0), 21 omitted faces per anchor entering as -(tau/3)W_f in normalized units delta=alpha/8; both signs |tau|<=10^-8, the -tau value a replay of the same |tau| formula; cover R={0,e_z} of the original xz Wilson loop, 48 links, 36 endpoints; observables A in B(H_R); common clock theta=alpha t/hbar with the window |theta|<=8, i.e. U=1 in the internal normalized time u=theta/8), with the two named construction families F1 = AQ1 centered whole-star boxes and F2 = I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding on the same Lambda_N=[-N,N]^3, N at least 2, with the Lieb-Robinson bound of Nachtergaele-Sims arXiv:1410.8174v1 Theorem 3.1, eqs. (51)-(52), quoted from the committed excerpt (PDF sha256 501af040512f2bdb62344ecbd093664e79ad1861338eabbce2c9791fca4e2fba), the unbounded on-site Casimirs h_b in the on-site slot of (44) and handled by the interaction picture, and the AQ1 constants F(r)=(1+r)^-4 on the coarse l1 metric, C<=224, ||Phi||_F<=2268|tau| for the whole-star interaction Phi (J=28|tau|, four incident stars) and ||Phi'||_F<=1323|tau| for the owner-set interaction Phi' (49 faces per site), substituted as upper bounds by monotonicity: (1) H^{F2,pad}_N minus H^{F1}_N is the sum of the 28N(5N+1) extra faces (enumerated on Lambda_2 to Lambda_5; per anchor 17, 13 and 5 faces when exactly one coordinate equals N, 10, 3 and 1 when two do, none at the corner), each charged once with norm |tau|/3, every owner on the outer layer at coarse l1 distance at least N-1 from e_z and at least N from 0 (both attained), plus the padding on-site terms, which factor out of the evolution exactly and are never charged. (2) Define b(N) = K_cmp (5N+1) N^-3 with K_cmp = 3969/155720800000000 (about 2.54879e-11; forward route: Duhamel with the inner F1 evolution, whole-star Phi, tier polynomial_lieb_robinson, route duhamel_inner_f1; margin about 2.354 against the frozen 6x10^-11). For the zero-selected patterned family at the same coupling |tau|<=10^-8 and every A in B(H_R) with ||A||<=1 on the fixed cover R, the finite-box Heisenberg evolutions T^{F1,N}_theta and T^{F2,N}_theta of the named construction families F1 and F2 on the same centered coarse cube Lambda_N satisfy ||T^{F2,N}_theta(A)-T^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| <= b(N) for |theta|<=8 in the common clock theta=alpha t/hbar; this is an algebraic comparison of the dynamics of the named constructions on a compact time window at a rate in N, not equality of GNS dynamics or of correlation functions of different states, not a uniform-in-time statement, and not a statement uniform in the lattice spacing a. The reverse route (Duhamel with the inner F2 evolution, owner-set Phi', route duhamel_inner_f2) proves the same inequality with the smaller labelled second-route constant K'_cmp = 452554889222515527/30481402343750000000000000000 (about 1.48469e-11, margin about 4.041); both constants are quadratic in tau (the first order vanishes because no extra face meets R), with exact tau/100 ratios 1953058850/194651 and 38176688920663121234473000000/3810205403940325763421973 inside the preregistered bracket [9500,10500]. (3) For F = F1 and F = F2, sup over M greater than N of ||T^{F,M}_theta(A)-T^{F,N}_theta(A)|| <= K_F/(N-1) ||A|| for |theta|<=8 and N at least 2, at the polynomial rate in N at fixed spacing: F1 with K_F1 = 9261/155720800000000 (about 5.94718e-11, forward, faces charged once, inner F1) and the second route 12128856933354903/118967041015625000000000000 (about 1.01951e-10, reverse, whole stars, inner F1 on Lambda_M); F2 with K_F2 = 117747/1245766400000000 (about 9.45177e-11, forward, one F1-inner Duhamel plus the comparison) and the second route 1055961408185869563/30481402343750000000000000000 (about 3.46428e-11, reverse, owner-set Phi', faces charged once); every value is at most the frozen 2.5x10^-10 (margins about 4.204, 2.452, 2.645 and 7.217); a bound for N to N+1 alone is not used as a Cauchy estimate. (4) Hence the F1 and F2 finite-box evolutions of every A in B(H_R) converge as whole sequences in norm, uniformly for |theta|<=8, and the F2 limit dynamics equals the AQ1 limit dynamics T_theta: ||T^{F2,N}_theta(A)-T_theta(A)|| <= min(K_F1, second-route K_F2)/(N-1) ||A||, and on every local algebra the same Duhamel sum with R replaced by a finite region tends to zero on every compact window, so the two automorphism groups agree on the quasi-local algebra. (5) AQ1 sections 4-5 are rerun for every subsequential F2 limit state with F2's own diagonal extraction (AY1): stationarity under T_theta, strong continuity of the GNS evolution and a nonnegative generator, with the physical cyclic space reducing it. Not admitted: equality of GNS dynamics or of correlation functions of different states, a common limit state or convergence of states, uniqueness of every infinite-volume ground state, translation invariance, any uniform-in-time statement, exponential decay in N with the polynomial Lieb-Robinson function, any rate or estimate in the lattice spacing a, a continuum or weak-coupling statement, and scientific priority.
loops.summary: The Heisenberg evolutions of local observables on the Wilson cover under the two named box constructions differ by at most about 2.5e-11 (5N+1)/N^3 on the window |theta| at most 8, each construction's evolutions form a Cauchy sequence in N at rate O(1/N), and the padded construction's limit dynamics is the AQ1 limit dynamics; the padded family's limit states satisfy the AQ1 stationarity and continuity statements.
limitations: Only the zero-selected patterned family (selected triple (0,0,0)), the cover R={0,e_z}, fixed spacing and |tau|<=10^-8, with the two named families F1 and F2 on centered cubes Lambda_N, N at least 2; nothing transfers to literal vertex boxes, periodic or orthant boxes, nonzero selected triples, the uniform route-B model, weak coupling or the continuum

Algebraic Heisenberg dynamics of the named constructions on a compact window only: no equality of GNS dynamics, no equality of correlation functions of different states, no common limit state and no convergence of states is established (F1 and F2 limit states remain subsequential and are not identified with each other); those need a proved common state (BB2)

The frozen constants hold for |theta|<=8 (U=1); the bounds grow like U^2/(1-vU/3) and nothing is claimed uniformly in time; outside the window only qualitative convergence on compact windows is used (for the O6 rerun)

Every rate is a rate in N at fixed spacing and strong bare coupling (a coarse step is (4a,2a,a)): order N^-2 for the comparison and 1/N for the Cauchy estimates with the polynomial F(r)=(1+r)^-4; no exponential decay in N is claimed, the optional exponential instance was not executed, and no estimate is uniform in the lattice spacing a

All constants are upper bounds: the admitted ||Phi||_F<=2268|tau| is four times the exact (48) supremum 567|tau| and ||Phi'||_F<=1323|tau| is 12.25 times 108|tau| (recorded, not used); the all-size face sum 168(5N+1)N^-3 is 20 to 31 times the enumerated sum at N=2 to 5

Inherited without re-proof: Nachtergaele-Sims Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 as transcribed in the committed excerpt (not machine-checked); AQ1's C<=224 and ||Phi||_F bounds (arithmetic re-verified); AM2's simple ground state and gap for F2 boxes and F2 compactness and diagonal extraction via AY1; the I1 dictionary; Stone's theorem, Fourier inversion and the tensor-product exponential of commuting self-adjoint operators on separate factors

Independence is limited: the contract, the selection note and the AY2 obligations table name the route and the constants; the routes differ in the inner family, the interaction indexing, the constants, the exponential remainder bound, the enumeration and the code; all agents are correlated model agents; both producers wrote their final files after the skeptic pre-comparison commit, so isolation is shown by disclosure and content, not by commit order

The producer checkers do not pin every labelled value: five silent source edits (labelled refinements, a retained weaker bound, preview strings) pass the producer checkers and are caught only by the skeptic value validator; the gate binds the exact rationals above
The -tau evaluations replay the same |tau| formula and are not a second confirmation
Scientific priority is unverified; the Lieb-Robinson and limit-dynamics theorems are credited to Nachtergaele-Sims and the O6 strategy to AQ1 (Gauvin arXiv:2503.15539v3 Supplement A.10)
loops.model: Zero-selected patterned family (AQ_patterned_zero_selected) at both signs |tau|<=10^-8; construction families F1 (AQ1 centered whole-star boxes) and F2 (I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding) on the same Lambda_N=[-N,N]^3, N at least 2; finite-box Heisenberg evolutions T^{F,N}_theta of A in B(H_R), cover R={0,e_z}, window |theta| at most 8 in theta=alpha t/hbar; l1 metric on the coarse factor lattice; Lieb-Robinson function F(r)=(1+r)^-4 with the AQ1 constants
derivation_steps: Write the F2-minus-F1 generator difference on Lambda_N as the 28N(5N+1) extra faces (enumerated and proved for all sizes) plus padding on-site terms that factor out exactly.

Apply Duhamel with the inner evolution bounded by the Nachtergaele-Sims Lieb-Robinson inequality (quoted verbatim from the committed excerpt) with the AQ1 whole-star constants (forward) or the owner-set constants (reverse); the first order vanishes because no extra face meets R.

loops.title: Hruday marginal locality of the reduced densities of the named constructions
loops.accepted: In the AM2/AQ1 zero-selected patterned family (model AQ_patterned_zero_selected: SU(2) Kogut-Susskind form on Z^3 at fixed spacing, coarse 24-link factors, selected triple exactly (0,0,0) with Haar product reference, 21 omitted faces per anchor entering as -(tau/3)W_f in normalized units delta=alpha/8; both signs |tau|<=10^-8; AM2 creation expansion with J<=28|tau|, R=1/64, G(t)=16e^{8t}(1+10t); cover R={0,e_z}; coarse l-infinity metric with star diameter 1; trace norm on B(H_Y)), with the named construction families F1 = AQ1 centered whole-star boxes Lambda_N=[-N,N]^3 and F2 = I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding on the same Lambda_N, N at least 2, and with the BA1 gate bound value K=49/111790368 used at every site of the union volume through the every-site form (b), proved in both packets: For the zero-selected patterned family at the same coupling |tau|<=10^-8, and for every comparison of the named construction families F1 and F2 on centered coarse cubes, the reduced densities of the finite-box ground vectors on the cover R differ by at most C q^(N-1) in trace norm, in each on-site cutoff space and, at fixed N, for the untruncated ground vectors, where N is the smaller box size; this is locality of the reduced densities of the named constructions at a rate in N, not uniqueness of any ground state, not a statement about other boundary conditions, and not a statement uniform in the lattice spacing a. Labelled secondary pair at q_2=151552|tau| with the re-instantiated input K_2=49/10202112 (disc radius 1/151552, proved in both packets): C_2=254713191786858884385903518855136871787/26288652445972361083565698627981857600000000 (about 9.6891e-06) and c_site,2=651079047656055039494458366725211/67298950261689244373928188487633555456 (about 9.6744e-06), iterated_split, meeting 1/20000 and 1/40000; polymer_kp proves the smaller values C_2 about 9.6440e-06 and c_site,2 about 9.6294e-06 (labelled). loops.summary: The reduced densities of the finite-box ground vectors of the two named box constructions differ on the Wilson cover by at most C q^(N-1) with q=1/64 and C about 8.9e-7, and on every finite region Y by at most c_site |Y| e^{|Y|/10^8} q^{d_Y} with c_site about 8.8e-7, for every comparison (nested boxes, the fixed-N change of boundary prescription, any two boxes, any two volumes of one prescription), at both signs, in each cutoff space and for the untruncated vectors; proved by a hard-core polymer expansion with a new mixed-weight lemma and independently by a recursive product-ordering split.
limitations: Scope: only the zero-selected patterned family (selected triple (0,0,0), Haar reference), fixed spacing, |tau|<=10^-8, the named families F1 and F2 on centered cubes Lambda_N with N at least 2, finite complete-factor volumes of one prescription containing Lambda_N, the cover R={0,e_z} and finite complete-factor regions inside Lambda_N; nothing transfers to other boundary conditions, nonzero selected triples, literal vertex boxes, weak coupling or the continuum; the constants are uniform in N at fixed spacing and in the cutoff, never in the lattice spacing.

Static statement about reduced densities of finite-box ground vectors per comparison: no dynamics, no limit object, no whole-sequence convergence or common limit (BB2), no translation statement, no uniqueness of any ground state and no analyticity of the reduced density in the coupling (no zero-free region is proved; the forward uses a real-parameter derivative and the reverse single-support telescoping).

The polymer_kp route uses the Kotecky-Preiss criterion (cited as Kotecky-Preiss 1986 in the form of Ueltschi 2004) as an external theorem that the frozen packet transcribes without a committed source excerpt (the plan rule that an external theorem is quoted from a committed excerpt with its PDF hash was not carried into the BB1 contract); its exploration-tree lemmas bound polymer sums, not the Ursell-weighted cluster sums behind Corollary 6.3 and Lemma 6.4. The citation was checked post hoc against the Ueltschi excerpt committed after the freeze (research/round33/sources/ueltschi-math-ph-0304003v3.md, arXiv:math-ph/0304003v3, PDF sha256 2cc3e036af5b2a46afe95acf0b5863fe5c7d31554debb10a2a5cade4122bdbfc; repair record bb1-kp-repair.md): with hard-core zeta in {0,-1}, c=0, b equal to the forward distance weight d and a(gamma)=a|supp gamma|, Theorem 3 (16) is the forward hypothesis, (19) gives its conclusion with the same weight e^{d(X)}, Theorem 1 gives the cluster expansion of every Z(Lambda'), and the test sets enter as mass-zero atoms; no factor is missing, so the cited statement and its use are covered. The excerpt is not a premise of the frozen packet, the original Kotecky-Preiss paper is neither committed nor needed, and every bound value is at least the value proved by the self-contained iterated_split route.

F2 volumes other than centred cubes (fifth comparison): the AY1 itemization H1-H5 is gated for F2 on Lambda_N; both producers apply it to every F2 volume containing Lambda_N as a local reading (on-site operator, per-anchor grouping inside the star, |X_b|<=4, per-site sum through b in u-S, cutoff compression), reviewed here as correct but not a gated statement.

Inherited without re-proof: the AM2 multilinear majorant, fixed point, uniqueness in the ball and section 6 facts; the AV1 product-ordering split, first-order coefficient (49 faces per site) and cutoff-vector removal F20-F23; the AY1 F2 itemization; the I1 dictionary; Banach, Weierstrass and the maximum principle are standard and not machine-checked. The every-site coefficient input (form (b)) and the secondary input K_2=49/10202112 are BB1 lemmas proved in both packets, not admitted BA1 statements.

Upper bounds only; the -tau values replay the same |tau| formula. The near term 2K(1+q)=3185/3577291776 is almost the whole headline constant (the far-site terms are about 10^-4 of C), so the constants are governed by the BA1 input; the region margin (about 2.28) is the binding one. The forward, reverse and skeptic derivations agree to within 2 parts in 10^4 on C and c_site.

Contract wording read as follows: at first order only supports contained in R move rho_R, and every straddling support, including the 6 of the 72 straddling faces that strictly contain R, has zero first-order R-marginal (D1); the lemma constant kappa_0 carries the factor |Y|; union-volume sites outside Lambda_N use the exponent (N-|u|_inf)_+=0; the reverse split weight is read as W<=1/(37888|tau|); tier, route and BA1 input are three separate labels.

Independence is limited to derivations, constants and code: the contract and selection note name both mechanisms and the frozen targets, the skeptic triage and pre-freeze review shaped the parameters, all agents are correlated model agents, isolation is verified for repository inputs only, and the reverse packet does not itself record its heredoc report write or the file names it saw.

loops.model: Zero-selected patterned family (AQ_patterned_zero_selected) at both signs |tau|<=10^-8; AM2 creation expansion (J<=28|tau|, R=1/64, G(t)=16e^{8t}(1+10t)) in each on-site cutoff space uniformly in the cutoff, then at fixed N for the untruncated ground vectors (AV1 F20-F23; AY1 itemization for F2); construction families F1 (AQ1 centered whole-star boxes) and F2 (I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding) on centered coarse cubes Lambda_N, N at least 2, and finite complete-factor volumes of one prescription containing Lambda_N; cover R={0,e_z} and finite complete-factor regions Y inside Lambda_N; coarse l-infinity metric on factor sites (star diameter 1); trace norm on B(H_Y)
derivation_steps: Write the reduced density through the AV1-type decomposition and prove the every-site form of the BA1 coefficient decay (every source term lies at distance at least N-|u| from each site u).

Forward: represent the norm and the marginal by hard-core polymers, prove the mixed-weight contraction lemma (loss w e^{4b} per interaction) and the Kotecky-Preiss condition with a = tau_bar^2; differentiate along a real parameter.
Reverse: telescope over single-support changes, use orthogonality at the changed support, recurse the split on covering regions and charge support sizes per site.
Sum the every-site coefficient input against the region's sites to obtain C q^(N-1) and the region form, uniformly in the cutoff, then remove the cutoff at fixed N.
applications: Input to whole-sequence convergence, the common limit and coarse translation invariance of the named constructions (BB2).
Marginal locality is a static per-comparison statement; it is not uniqueness of any ground state.

loops.title: Hruday whole-sequence convergence and common limit of the named constructions
loops.accepted: In the AM2/AQ1 zero-selected patterned family (model AQ_patterned_zero_selected: SU(2) Kogut-Susskind form on Z^3 at fixed spacing, coarse 24-link factors, selected triple exactly (0,0,0) with Haar product reference, 21 omitted faces per anchor entering as -(tau/3)W_f in normalized units delta=alpha/8; both signs |tau|<=10^-8; AM2 creation expansion in each on-site cutoff space; cover R={0,e_z}; coarse l-infinity metric with star diameter 1 for states and l1 on the coarse factor lattice with F(r)=(1+r)^-4 for dynamics; trace norm on B(H_Y); clock theta=alpha t/hbar), with the named construction families F1 = AQ1 centered whole-star boxes Lambda_N=[-N,N]^3 and F2 = I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding on the same Lambda_N, N at least 2, with the BA2 gate dynamics constants, and with the BB1 hypotheses discharged by the BB1 gate (sha256 18141fea672e5bae09024a5fddc56ea7102aae56ecca16fbb30d67a1354a3827, accepted_within_scope), which admits for each of the five comparisons c1-c5 of the BB1 contract, at both signs, in each on-site cutoff space with constants independent of the cutoff and at fixed N for the untruncated ground vectors, the R form C q^(N-1) with q=1/64 and C about 8.9051e-07 (polymer_kp bound value; iterated_split 8.9043e-07), at most C_h=1/250000, and the region form c_site |Y| e^{|Y|/10^8} q^{d_Y} with c_site about 8.7681e-07 (iterated_split 8.7673e-07), at most c_h=1/500000, so that every hypothesis used by either route is discharged: For the zero-selected patterned family at the same coupling |tau|<=10^-8, under the BB1 locality bounds at their frozen targets as hypotheses (discharged only when the BB1 gate admits constants at most those targets), the reduced densities of the named construction families F1 and F2 on centered coarse cubes converge as whole sequences, at a rate in N, to one common limit on every finite region; this limit coincides with every AQ1 subsequential limit and every F2 subsequential limit, is invariant under coarse translations, and has as correlation functions on |theta|<=8 the limits of the finite-box correlation functions; this is convergence of the named constructions, not uniqueness of any ground state, not a statement about states outside the named constructions, and not a statement uniform in the lattice spacing a. Constants (exact; both signs; F1 and F2; in each on-site cutoff space uniformly in the cutoff and, at fixed N, for the untruncated ground vectors; evaluated at the hypothesis values as the contract target specifies, and valid under the discharge because each is nondecreasing in the BB1 constants). Item 1: sup over M greater than N of ||rho^{F,M}_R-rho^{F,N}_R||_1 <= C' q^(N-1) with C'=4/984375 (about 4.0635e-06; exact_first_order, nested_telescoping, hypothesis source bb1_frozen_targets, BB1 route polymer_kp; margin 315/128 against 1/100000), and for every finite complete-factor region Y inside Lambda_N, sup over M greater than N of ||rho^{F,M}_Y-rho^{F,N}_Y||_1 <= c'_site |Y| e^{|Y|/10^8} q^{d_Y} with d_Y=N-max_{y in Y}|y|_inf and c'_site=2/984375 (about 2.0317e-06; margin 315/128 against 1/200000); the union_comparison route proves C'=1/250000 and c'_site=1/500000 (labelled); re-evaluated at the admitted BB1 values (labelled, not bound), C' is about 9.0465e-07 and c'_site about 8.9073e-07 (nested_telescoping), about 8.9051e-07 and 8.7681e-07 (union_comparison). The limit on every finite region follows from this Cauchy bound and trace-class completeness, without compactness. Item 2: the F1 and F2 limits coincide on every finite region (BB1 comparison c3, the fixed-N comparison of the two prescriptions). Item 3: the limit equals every AQ1 subsequential limit (F1) and every F2 subsequential limit on every finite region and inherits exactly the admitted properties of those states: AQ1 stationarity under T_theta, strong continuity of the GNS evolution and a nonnegative generator (for F2 limits through BA2's rerun of AQ1 sections 4-5), and the AQ2 statement for the actual AQ1 centered subsequential state, H_phys at least (alpha/16)(I-P_Omega) with a simple vacuum on the invariant-local cyclic completion, the full-GNS strengthening only as qualified in the AQ2 gate. Item 4: for every coarse translation v (fine translation (4v_x,2v_y,v_z), preserving residues and face classes) and N at least |v|_inf+2, ||rho^{Lambda_N+v}_R-rho^{Lambda_N}_R||_1 <= C_h q^(N-|v|_inf-1) with C_h=1/250000 (the direct BB1 comparison c5 of two one-prescription volumes containing Lambda_{N-|v|_inf}; re-evaluated at the admitted C about 8.9051e-07, labelled; a two-step comparison through the union is labelled only), and the limit is invariant under coarse translations on every finite region (region form of c5); non-coarse translations are rejected. Item 5: for N at least 5, r_N=floor((N-1)/2), |theta| at most 8 and A in B(H_R), |c^{F,N}_A(theta)-c^inf_A(theta)| <= ||A||^2 [C_dyn/(r_N-1) + c'_site |Lambda_{r_N}| e^{|Lambda_{r_N}|/10^8} q^(N-r_N) + 2C' q^(N-1)] with complex-mean centering, c^{F,N}_A(theta)=omega^{F,N}(A* T^{F,N}_theta(A))-|omega^{F,N}(A)|^2 and c^inf_A(theta)=omega_inf(A* T_theta(A))-|omega_inf(A)|^2, and C_dyn=78057/622883200000000 (about 1.2532e-10; polynomial_lieb_robinson, duhamel_inner_f1, 2K_F1+K_cmp/4 from the BA2 gate values, one constant for both families; margin about 3.99 against 1/2000000000); the reverse per-family values 9261/77860400000000 (F1, duhamel_inner_f1, about 1.1894e-10) and 1055961408185869563/15240701171875000000000000000 (F2, duhamel_inner_f2, about 6.9286e-11) are labelled. This inequality holds for every N at least 5. It gives an explicit rate in N only on the certified range 5<=N<=14000, where N |c^{F,N}_A(theta)-c^inf_A(theta)| <= K5 ||A||^2 with K5 about 6.10e-09 (about 5.96e-09 and 5.46e-09 with the reverse F1 and F2 constants); no O(1/N) rate is asserted beyond that range. The bracket stays below 2 up to N=14418 and is at least 2 at N=14419 and at every larger N, so the bound is vacuous from N=14419 (certified here at the hypothesis values and at the admitted values alike; the historical assistant-2 found the same first exceedance independently at the hypothesis values). The finite-box correlation functions converge to c^inf_A(theta) along the whole sequence of N, for every A in B(H_R) and |theta| at most 8, without a rate outside the certified range (the inequality with any fixed r in place of r_N gives a limsup of at most C_dyn/(r-1) ||A||^2). Labelled secondary at q_2=151552|tau| (592/390625 at the cap): C'_2=625/12481056 (about 5.0076e-05, target 1/8000) and c'_site,2=625/24962112 (about 2.5038e-05, no target), discharged by the BB1 secondary pair (C_2 about 9.689e-06 at most 1/20000 and c_site,2 about 9.674e-06 at most 1/40000, iterated_split bound values). The tau to tau/100 ratios are exactly 1 for C' and c'_site at the hypothesis values (non-discriminating), 1953058850/194651 (about 10033.64) for C_dyn and the reverse F1 value, about 10019.59 for the reverse F2 value, 1085053/1083425 (about 1.0015) for C'_2, and exactly 100 for q_2. Rates are per coarse step in N at fixed spacing.
loops.summary: The reduced densities of both named box constructions converge along the whole sequence of box sizes, at the rate q^(N-1) with q=1/64 and C' about 4.1e-6, to one common limit on every finite region; the limit coincides with every earlier subsequential limit of either family, inherits their admitted stationarity, GNS and gap properties, is invariant under coarse translations, and its correlation functions on |theta|<=8 are the limits of the finite-box ones (rate 1/N on 5<=N<=14000; convergence without a rate beyond).
limitations: Scope: only the zero-selected patterned family (selected triple (0,0,0), Haar reference), fixed spacing, |tau|<=10^-8, the named families F1 and F2 on centered cubes Lambda_N with N at least 2 and the limit of the named constructions, the cover R and finite complete-factor regions, coarse translations and the window |theta|<=8; nothing transfers to other boundary conditions, states outside the named constructions, nonzero selected triples, literal vertex boxes, weak coupling or the continuum; the constants are uniform in N at fixed spacing and in the cutoff, never in the lattice spacing.

Convergence of the named constructions only: no uniqueness of any ground state and no statement about any other infinite-volume state; the limit is identified only with the AQ1 and F2 subsequential limits and inherits only the listed admitted properties (the full-GNS strengthening only as qualified in the AQ2 gate); no equality of GNS dynamics of different states and no uniform-in-time statement.

Discharge: both routes prove items 1-5 from the BB1 frozen targets C_h=1/250000 and c_h=1/500000 at q=1/64 as hypotheses. The BB1 gate (sha256 18141fea672e5bae09024a5fddc56ea7102aae56ecca16fbb30d67a1354a3827, commit eef57b4) admits C about 8.9051e-07 and c_site about 8.7681e-07 for all five comparisons, both forms, both cutoff regimes and both signs. The skeptic discharge (the protocol committed in bb2_check.py before either producer or the gate was read, applied to the anchored admission record bb2-bb1-admission.json and cross-checked with the BB1 review table in 40 cells) finds every item full and every cell of both producers' hypothesis maps discharged. The bound constants are evaluated at the hypothesis values; the values re-evaluated at the admitted constants are labelled only.

The discharge carries the BB1 limitations: the polymer_kp bound values rest on the Kotecky-Preiss criterion, whose citation was checked post hoc against the committed Ueltschi excerpt and found covered; the self-contained iterated_split values discharge every item as well (labelled run). F2 volumes other than centred cubes in c5 (item 4) rest on the AY1 itemization as a reviewed local reading, not a gated statement.

Item-5 rate (reverse W1; skeptic defect D12): contract required item 5 says the rate in N is O(1/N), but with r_N and the region form frozen the region term on Lambda_{r_N} carries e^{|Lambda_{r_N}|/10^8} with |Lambda_{r_N}| about N^3, which eventually outgrows q^(N-r_N). The rate holds only on the certified range 5<=N<=14000 and the bound is vacuous from N=14419, so that clause of the requirement is met on the certified range only. The skeptic's own pre-comparison derivation (section 8) stated the rate without the range, and its pre-freeze and pre-comparison reviews missed the defect; the reverse producer found it.

Rejected forward overclaim: the forward report's rate paragraph (the rate in N is O(1/N) while the state terms decay geometrically in N, the cube volume growing only like N^3) and the matching results text are rejected, because the region term is at least 2 from N=14419 on; the forward checker evaluates item 5 only for N<=59, and its enclosure e^x<=1/(1-x) is unusable from N=465. The forward's item-5 inequality and constants are correct; the frozen forward files are retained as evidence and the rejected wording enters no gate text.

Constants are upper bounds only; the minus-sign values replay the same |tau| formula. C' and c'_site at the hypothesis values do not depend on tau (ratio exactly 1, non-discriminating); the linear tau-scaling of the BB1 constants is recorded by BB1 (about 100.648). The dynamics constant is BA2's, and the correlation bound holds per fixed local A on |theta|<=8 only.

Contract wording read as follows: union_comparison is one direct application of c4 or c5 (a two-step comparison through a third volume is labelled, and the reverse's labelled item-4 fallback 2C_h is valid but looser than the available C_h(1+q^|v|)); C_dyn is bound as the forward's single-route constant with the reverse per-family values labelled (D3, D10); c'_site,2 has no target (D5); d_Y is the BB1 definition (D7); no frame for limited outcomes (D9, moot at this verdict); several inherited control texts were written for BA2 or BB1 (D6); the item-3 inheritance is read within the admitted scope (D4, D11).

Independence is limited to derivations, constants and code: all agents are correlated model agents; the frozen targets, the brackets and the conditional semantics came from the skeptic's BB pre-freeze review; the skeptic pre-comparison package was committed after the forward commit and before the reverse commit; isolation is verified for repository inputs only, and both producers disclosed name-only exposures to other agents' file names.
Scientific priority is unverified.
loops.model: Zero-selected patterned family (AQ_patterned_zero_selected) at both signs |tau|<=10^-8; construction families F1 (AQ1 centered whole-star boxes) and F2 (I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding) on centered coarse cubes Lambda_N, N at least 2, and their limit on every finite complete-factor region; states in trace norm on B(H_Y) with the coarse l-infinity metric; dynamics T_theta and T^{F,N}_theta with the l1 metric and F(r)=(1+r)^-4 on |theta| at most 8, theta=alpha t/hbar; each on-site cutoff space uniformly in the cutoff, then the untruncated ground vectors at fixed N; BB1 locality bounds as hypotheses discharged by the BB1 gate (sha256 18141fea672e5bae09024a5fddc56ea7102aae56ecca16fbb30d67a1354a3827)
derivation_steps: Take the BB1 locality bounds at their frozen targets as hypotheses and sum consecutive comparisons (forward, geometric factor 1/(1-q)) or compare directly through the larger cube (reverse) to obtain the whole-sequence Cauchy estimate over all M>N and the limit without compactness.
Use the fixed-N comparison of the two boundary prescriptions to identify the two limits, and the subsequence property to identify the limit with every AQ1 and F2 subsequential limit.
Compare Lambda_N+v with Lambda_N through Lambda_{N-|v|} for coarse translations; check non-coarse translations face by face.
Combine the BA2 dynamics comparison on Lambda_{r_N} with the region-form state bound to bound correlation-function differences, and discharge every hypothesis against the BB1 gate item by item.
applications: Closes AY2 obligations O2 (whole-sequence convergence), O3 (coarse translation invariance) and O4 (a rate in N) for the named constructions; uniqueness of ground states (O1) stays open.
Makes the Round32 node and sign certificates statements about one limit of the named constructions (BC1).
